summary.intent: Close the caliper-docgen v1 alpha gap: establish a baseline, ship a schema v4 batch (readonly, index signatures, RefObject), fix shadcn/antd recall gaps, add shape-based detection, and harden on-demand TS 7.1. Session began with reading docs, restating the definition of done, and getting the user's yes.
summary.outcome: After the user approved the definition of done, the assistant cleaned up old branches, dispatched the baseline weekly run, created four trails (#125-#128), and implemented schema v4 in a worktree. Core types, resolvers, docs, TS readers, a changeset and exact-prop-set tests were done; lint and tests passed, bench was within noise, and a signed commit was made. The PR, trail link, baseline comparison and steps 3-6 remain.

repo: Local checkout was stale at first: docs/measurement.md and scripts/weekly.py appeared missing until origin was fetched. Verify main's tip after fetching before trusting the local tree.
ADR 0023 / the schema v3 commit is the template for a schema bump: core types, cache golden fixture, snapshots, TS schema readers, trycmd, a changeset and serialization-formats.md.
Snapshot tests resolve @types/react via node_modules, so a fresh worktree needs its own install or snapshots show path noise and a spurious `key` prop.
Keeping index signatures as object fields made consumers that read object fields as props (props-base code) emit a bogus prop named `key`; those consumers must filter index-signature fields.
The existing union normalizer drops `| undefined` from values, so exact-prop-set tests must expect the plain type.
Extractor sites that match `Array` with a wildcard fallback silently miss the new `Readonly` wrapper; readonly must be peeled in declared const values.

Hand-maintained typings (packages/napi/index.d.ts, packages/storybook/src/schema.ts, packages/vite-plugin/src/schema.ts) and the crates/semantic converter must be updated along with core for a PropType change.
Repo lint recipes run clippy without --all-targets; `just bench` compares against origin/main.

code.finding: New file with exact-prop-set tests for readonly, index signatures and RefObject, following the rule of new tests in new files.
The golden fixture for cache bytes was extended to cover the new shapes, and its snapshot regenerated.

workflow: Bisect an unexpected snapshot diff by toggling one change (peel readonly) and re-running snapshots, which isolated the index-signature cause.
Compare against baseline code in the same environment, by saving a patch and re-running, to tell your own regressions from environment noise.
Use small Python scripts in the job tmp dir for mechanical edits and diffs, since the harness requires literal script paths and shell loops are discouraged.
Run the compiler-driven loop (change core types, follow the non-exhaustive match errors) for enum-shape changes.

friction: Local main was behind origin, so the first listing of docs and scripts was misleading.
Two agent worktrees had uncommitted files and could not be cleaned up automatically.
The worktree lacked node_modules, which produced misleading snapshot diffs and cost a bisect.
Many test struct literals needed mechanical patching for the new fields.
The harness required literal script paths, so scripts were written into the job tmp dir.
open_items: Record baseline numbers from weekly run 41159666463 (recall, time, RSS, oracle wrong-rate) and set concrete targets.
Link the schema-v4 branch to its trail with `entire trail link`, then fill in the draft PR and mark it ready; do not approve trails.
Step 3: root-cause the shadcn (39.5%) and antd (80.3%) recall gaps, including whether PurePanel is a pairing bug.
Step 4: shape-based detection (memo(forwardRef) without type args, import-source matching, {Name}Props heuristic, Chakra NonNullable<union>).
Step 5: on-demand TS 7.1 hardening (version range plus self-check, memory cap, real-tsc CI test, latency re-measure).
Step 6: re-run weekly, compare with the baseline, and update STATUS.md and the site numbers.
Two leftover agent worktrees with uncommitted files need a decision.
Housekeeping the user owns: delete scratch remote branches, remove tap secrets, close stale Entire trails.
